probes.name: B0-comment-only-GREEN-control
probes.subject: services/engine/llm/capacity.py
probes.old: #: Characters per generated token, measured across PLAN-0118's arms as
probes.new: #: Characters per generated token (control mutation), measured across PLAN-0118's arms as
probes.note: 🟢 The battery's own control. Editing a comment must change nothing, so a RED here would mean every reading below is measuring something other than the mutation it names. An uncontrolled instrument does not fail loudly, it fails confidently (Lesson #0056).

probes.name: B1-a-constrained-call-is-not-called-structuring
probes.subject: services/engine/llm/capacity.py
probes.note: 🔴 The schema-constrained call stops being recognised as one. Budgets chosen per shape would then be applied to the wrong shape, which is the single thing the derivation exists to prevent.

probes.name: B2-a-thinking-call-is-not-called-reasoning
probes.subject: services/engine/llm/capacity.py
probes.note: 🔴 The reasoning pass -- the expensive one, the one PLAN-0118 measured at an order of magnitude more demand -- becomes indistinguishable from a plain generation.

probes.name: B3-an-unadorned-call-is-misread-as-reasoning
probes.subject: services/engine/llm/capacity.py
probes.note: 🔴 The opposite error to B2, and the reason 'plain' exists as a third value rather than being folded into 'reasoning': over-classifying every unadorned call would inflate its budget on the basis of reasoning it never does.

probes.name: B4-precedence-inverts-when-both-arguments-are-set
probes.subject: services/engine/llm/capacity.py
probes.new: if response_format is not None and think is None:
probes.note: 🔴 The realistic version of this defect: not a wrong branch but a wrong PRECEDENCE. Pattern B call 2 with `think` left on would be classified reasoning, and B1's claim stays GREEN under it because that case sets no `think` -- which is what makes the attribution exact.

probes.name: B5-a-falsey-think-reads-as-absent
probes.subject: services/engine/llm/capacity.py
probes.note: 🔴 The exact mistake Ollama #18044 punishes: `think: false` disables the thinking PARSER, not the thinking GENERATION, so a truthiness test under-budgets precisely the calls still paying for a reasoning pass.

probes.name: B6-the-shipped-models-decode-rate-drifts
probes.subject: services/engine/llm/capacity.py
probes.note: 🔴 The one genuinely MEASURED term in the table, on the only model any published system runs. A drift here silently re-prices every budget decision downstream.

probes.name: B7-an-unmeasured-model-is-quietly-defaulted
probes.subject: services/engine/llm/capacity.py
probes.note: 🔴 SD-2 = (b) replaced by the failure mode it was ruled against: serving an unmeasured model under some OTHER model's capacity. Every number the budget rule produced would then be about a model that is not running.

probes.name: B8-the-refusal-does-not-name-the-model
probes.subject: services/engine/llm/capacity.py
probes.old: f"model {model!r} has no measured serving capacity; "
probes.new: f"a model has no measured serving capacity; "
probes.note: 🔴 Aimed so B7's claim stays GREEN: it still raises, so pytest reaches this second assertion. A refusal that does not say WHICH model it refused is unactionable in a process binding several (Lesson #0043 -- a RED must name what broke).

probes.name: B9-the-refusal-is-swallowed-into-a-fallback
probes.subject: services/engine/llm/capacity.py
probes.note: 🔴 The refusal is swallowed by an early fallback return -- the raise below it becomes unreachable. ⚠️ An earlier draft of this probe swapped `except KeyError` for `except ZeroDivisionError`, letting a bare KeyError escape. That is a NON-assertion exception, which the driver classifies CRASHED and credits nothing: the probe would have witnessed nothing while looking like it had. The same trap is documented on B23. A mutation aimed at a `pytest.raises` claim must make the code raise NOTHING, never raise something else.

probes.name: B10-the-refusal-hides-what-would-have-worked
probes.subject: services/engine/llm/capacity.py
probes.note: 🔴 B9's claim stays GREEN here -- it still raises the right type -- so pytest reaches this one. An error that sends the reader to the source to discover what WAS acceptable has given up the one job an error message has.

probes.name: B11-a-second-models-rate-drifts
probes.subject: services/engine/llm/capacity.py
probes.note: 🔴 Deliberately a TINY drift, on a model B6 does not touch. The pin has to catch a plausible typo, not only an obvious replacement -- 19.6 for 19.5 is what a careless edit actually looks like.

probes.name: B12-a-model-key-is-mistyped
probes.subject: services/engine/llm/capacity.py
probes.note: 🔴 The POSITIVE CONTROL of a negative test. The two assertions after it are 'nothing claims to be measured' -- satisfied vacuously by an empty or wrong table -- so this membership check is what stops those from passing on nothing.

probes.name: B13-the-measured-term-stops-saying-it-is-measured
probes.subject: services/engine/llm/capacity.py
probes.note: 🔴 The second positive control of the same test, and it needs its own probe because pytest stops at the first failed assert -- B12 reddens the membership check and could never reach this one. The membership claim stays GREEN here, which is what makes the attribution exact.

probes.name: B14-a-provisional-term-promotes-itself-to-measured
probes.subject: services/engine/llm/capacity.py
probes.note: 🔴 THE tripwire for Step 4b, and the failure the whole s287 posture exists to prevent: a stand-in hardening into a fact with nobody noticing. Both earlier assertions in this test stay GREEN under it, so this exact claim is what reddens.

probes.name: B15-a-provisional-term-goes-missing-from-the-count
probes.subject: services/engine/llm/capacity.py
probes.note: 🔴 The positive control for the naming check below: 'every provisional term names its replacement' is vacuously true of ZERO provisional terms, so the count has to be pinned before the property means anything.

probes.name: B16-a-stand-in-does-not-name-what-replaces-it
probes.subject: services/engine/llm/capacity.py
probes.note: 🔴 B15's count claim stays GREEN -- the term is still provisional, just anonymous -- so pytest reaches this one. A stand-in whose replacement is unnamed is a stand-in nobody will retire.

probes.name: B17-a-model-claims-full-measurement-early
probes.subject: services/engine/llm/capacity.py
probes.note: 🔴 `fully_measured` is what gates whether a budget verdict can be trusted. Hard-coding it True makes every verdict present itself as measured while three of its four terms are still guesses.

probes.name: B18-the-budget-rule-always-says-yes
probes.subject: services/engine/llm/capacity.py
probes.note: 🔴 AC-4's named failing case. A rule that cannot refuse is not a rule, and this is the mutation that proves the criterion is not closing on a formality.

probes.name: B19-the-budget-rule-always-says-no
probes.subject: services/engine/llm/capacity.py
probes.note: 🔴 The other direction, and the reason both are needed: a rule stuck on 'no' passes B18's test perfectly. This claim is also the one that documents WHY the posture ruled at s287 matters -- the same case flips to fitting the moment the unmeasured terms are treated as zero.

probes.name: B20-the-decode-rate-is-applied-inverted
probes.subject: services/engine/llm/capacity.py
probes.note: 🔴 AC-4's PASSING case, which needs its own probe: a rule that refuses everything would satisfy every failing-case test in this module. This is the arm Step 6 is aiming at, so a false refusal here would block the experiment programme rather than protect it.

probes.name: B21-equality-is-treated-as-fitting
probes.subject: services/engine/llm/capacity.py
probes.note: 🔴 The realistic boundary defect, and not a pedantic one: the timeout ABORTS and discards every token already produced, so a projection landing exactly on the deadline is a total loss rather than a near miss. `<=` looks tidier and is wrong.

probes.name: B22-the-verdict-drops-a-term-it-was-given
probes.subject: services/engine/llm/capacity.py
probes.note: 🔴 CLAUDE.md section 8: a report prints the values it measured, never a bare verdict. A verdict that silently zeroes a term it was handed makes every disagreement a hunt instead of one step.

probes.name: B23-a-corrupt-rate-gets-a-plausible-answer
probes.subject: services/engine/llm/capacity.py
probes.note: 🔴 Mutates the MESSAGE rather than the guard, deliberately: removing the guard raises ZeroDivisionError, which the driver classifies CRASHED and credits nothing. This keeps the failure an assertion failure, so the probe witnesses instead of merely crashing.

probes.name: B24-a-provisional-verdict-presents-itself-as-measured
probes.subject: services/engine/llm/capacity.py
probes.note: 🔴 The seam between the pure rule and the posture. `fits_in_timeout` leaves terms_measured True because it cannot know; if `evaluate_budget` forgets to narrow it, every caller is told a guess is a measurement.

probes.name: B25-todays-shipped-cap-stops-fitting
probes.subject: services/engine/llm/capacity.py
probes.note: 🔴 The regression floor in arithmetic form. If the shipped configuration stops projecting as servable, the seam has broken CURRENT behaviour -- a defect in the seam, not a discovery about budgets.

probes.name: B26-zeroing-the-unmeasured-load-lets-the-refused-case-pass
probes.subject: services/engine/llm/capacity.py
probes.note: 🔴 THE probe that priced the s287 ruling. AC-4 requires a case that FAILS, and this shows the failure is carried entirely by the provisional load term: with it zeroed, qwen at 2048 projects 105.0s against a 120s timeout and FITS. A posture treating unmeasured terms as zero could not have closed AC-4 at all -- measured before the ruling, not argued.

probes.name: B27-the-table-lookup-is-bypassed
probes.subject: services/engine/llm/capacity.py
probes.note: 🔴 SD-2's refusal reaching the caller. A hard-coded lookup would answer for EVERY model with one model's capacity -- and answer plausibly, which is worse than failing.

probes.name: B28-the-prompt-estimate-counts-only-content
probes.subject: services/engine/llm/capacity.py
probes.old: characters = sum(len(value) for message in messages for value in message.values())
probes.new: characters = sum(len(m.get("content", "")) for m in messages)
probes.note: 🔴 Under-stating the prompt is the UNSAFE direction: every serialised field occupies context, and a short estimate delays the explicit num_ctx past the point where the prompt starts being truncated invisibly.

probes.name: B29-a-short-prompt-estimates-as-zero-tokens
probes.subject: services/engine/llm/capacity.py
probes.note: 🔴 Rounding down instead of up. A zero-token prompt tells the headroom check the entire context window is free for generation -- the estimator's one job, inverted, on the shortest inputs.

probes.name: B30-the-context-trigger-is-stuck-on
probes.subject: services/engine/llm/capacity.py
probes.note: 🔴 The positive control for AC-5's arithmetic: 'the trigger fires when it should' is worth nothing unless 'it stays quiet when it should' can fail. 741 + 1024 is well inside 4096, which is why AC-5 is dormant on today's shipped configuration.

probes.name: B31-the-context-trigger-is-stuck-off
probes.subject: services/engine/llm/capacity.py
probes.note: 🔴 Step 6's arm, unprotected: a 741-token prompt plus a 4096 cap does not fit a 4096 window, and a trigger stuck off means the PROMPT is truncated rather than the output -- invisible to done_reason, the oracle this PLAN rests on.

probes.name: B32-the-window-stops-covering-prompt-plus-cap
probes.subject: services/engine/llm/capacity.py
probes.note: 🔴 AC-5's literal guarantee. The assertion sweeps five (prompt, cap) shapes in ONE claim precisely so a constant implementation cannot pass by luck on a small case -- the large-prompt case is what this mutation reddens.
